originality.rationale: The exact maximum for the (2,3) forbidden-overlap interval is not implied by the earlier (1,k) optima: the length-one restriction changes the admissible codes. Stanovnik's general boundary reduction leaves a separate six-bit extremum and the accessible 2025 (t1,t2) paper establishes construction family sizes without the unrestricted sharp bound. The present 10-vertex product optimum is established by new explicit four-state arc inequalities; broad and targeted comparisons with published research records returned no covering statement. An inaccessible potentially related construction paper is noted as residual risk.

value.rationale: Sharp capacity for the first natural consecutive overlap interval excluding length one; resolves all n>=6, beyond earlier size-of-construction and general bounds. The 10-word optimal boundary gives 10/64 of available six-bit patterns, compared with six for the stricter (1,3) restriction. Frame-synchronization applications motivate precise restricted-overlap capacity; the four-state extremal inequality supplies a genuine structural reason rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
